explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/977: the main question asks whether P(2^n − 1)/n → ∞, and 'In [Er65b] Erdős also asks about P(n!+1)'; the page adds that this case appears to be open, with Murty–Wong's conditional (1+o(1)) n log n and Lai's limsup ≥ 1 + 9 log 2. The Lean statement Tendsto (n ↦ maxPrimeFac(n!+1)/n) atTop atTop is the direct analogue of the main question for n!+1, which is the natural reading of 'also asks about P(n!+1)' and is consistent with the cited partial results. Nat.maxPrimeFac is the greatest prime factor. Faithful.
